headline: Bangladesh's gross reserves cross $37 billion again
summary: The country's total reserves rose to $37.066 billion, while the IMF's BPM6 calculation stands at $32.260 billion.
details: Bangladesh's total (gross) reserves have increased to $37.066 billion within a single day, according to recent data.
Under the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) BPM6 calculation method, the reserves currently stand at $32.260 billion.
On Monday, August 10, the gross reserves were $36.96 billion, and the BPM6 reserves were $32.15 billion.
The BPM6 method is widely considered one of the most acceptable international standards for measuring a country's usable foreign exchange reserves.
This increase comes amid various measures taken by the central bank to maintain stability in the foreign exchange sector and the currency market.
According to Bangladesh Bank data, the BPM6 reserves had already crossed the $32 billion mark on Tuesday, August 11.

headline: Nationwide order: Shops and malls to close by 8pm
summary: A new directive requires all retail outlets and shopping centers across Bangladesh to shut their doors by 8 PM.
details: All shops and shopping malls across Bangladesh have been directed to close by 8 PM nationwide.
The directive includes a specific instruction for billboards to be turned off by 7 PM.
This new decision regarding the operational hours of retail outlets and shopping centers aims to regulate business timings across the country.
The order applies to all types of retail establishments, ensuring a uniform closing time for shopping malls and individual shops.
